svg.text: Bleeding after birth: feel the uterus before you do anything else
One examination separates the four causes
She is bleeding. Put a hand on the fundus.
Soft and high, or firm and central? The answer sends you down two different roads.
SOFT uterus — the muscle is not gripping
This is tone, and it causes most postpartum
haemorrhage in Ghana.
Rub up a contraction with the fundus
Empty the bladder — a full one blocks it
Uterotonic as prescribed
Two large cannulae, blood taken and sent
Massage works in seconds and costs nothing
FIRM uterus — the muscle is doing its job
So the blood is coming from somewhere else.
Trauma — look for a tear
Cervix, vagina, perineum. Bright red, steady,
continuing through a hard uterus.
Tissue — check the placenta is complete
Thrombin — blood not clotting anywhere
More oxytocin will not close a tear
Why the loss is always underestimated
Blood soaks into linen, runs onto the floor,
and collects inside the uterus unseen.
A young woman keeps a normal blood
pressure until she is very nearly empty.
Watch the pulse and the fundal height.
Prevention, at every single birth
A uterotonic within one minute of birth
Controlled cord traction with the uterus
guarded by the other hand
Examine the placenta and membranes
Then keep feeling the fundus for two hours
